newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BLATTER RULES OUT MORE BREAKS FOR TELEVISION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BLATTER RULES OUT MORE BREAKS FOR TELEVISION.

text.p: FIFA general secretary Sepp Blatter has ruled out the introduction of more breaks in soccer to help television boost advertising revenue.

"Splitting the game into thirds or quarters is definitely not going to happen," Blatter wrote in the German sports magazine Kicker. "There are also going to be no time-outs in the game in the foreseeable future."

Bosses at German television stations RTL and Sat1 sparked a debate this week when they warned that the high cost of rights meant soccer would soon be available only on pay-per-view TV unless they could pull in more advertising revenue.
Bayern Munich chairman Franz Beckenbauer dismissed the whole discussion "as useful as a hole in the head" and "the nonsense of the century".

Blatter said he had had the original idea about basketball-type time-outs last year to help coaches have more influence on the game. But tests in some competitions and countries in 1995 had not been positive.
"For TV it would be a wonderful opportunity to put in extra advertising but our tests have shown that the distances in football are too large," Blatter said.

"It takes too long for the players to get together, the coach to give his instructions and the players to get back into position... Tests in Sweden and Brazil have shown that the flow of the game also suffers."
